new_entities.name: Acute nicotine gum
new_entities.description: Acute administration of nicotine gum used to test short-term psychostimulant and cognitive effects.

new_entities.name: Working memory
new_entities.description: The ability to temporarily hold and manipulate information over short time periods.

edges.population: healthy non-smokers, never-smokers, or abstinent smokers receiving acute nicotine gum doses
edges.mechanism: Nicotine stimulates nicotinic acetylcholine receptors and can sharpen attentional signaling, which may indirectly help some working-memory tasks. Across human gum studies, though, the clearest and most reproducible effects are on vigilance or attention, while working-memory gains are inconsistent and often absent.
edges.summary: Acute nicotine gum does not show a reliable broad working-memory benefit in humans. Some studies report task-specific improvements, but others find no meaningful working-memory change despite clear physiological or attentional effects, so the most honest read is mixed.
edges.caveats: Any cognitive effect has to be weighed against nicotine's obvious dependence liability and cardiovascular stimulation. This is not a clean lifestyle nootropic edge even where small task benefits appear.

evidence.citation: Trimmel M et al 2005 Psychol Addict Behav
